State machine parser for tar snapshots, manifests, status cache, and account data.

# Purpose
`fd_ssparse.c` implements a streaming parser for a sparse snapshot archive format. It reads a TAR-like input one chunk at a time and advances through a fixed state machine that handles the archive header, the `version` file, the `snapshots/` manifest, the `snapshots/status_cache` file, and account append-vector files under `accounts/`. The parser validates TAR metadata, checks file names and sizes, and enforces the expected file order. It also tracks parse progress with byte counters and returns detailed advance results for each state.

The file also manages parser setup and shared memory layout. Functions such as [`fd_ssparse_align`](<#fd_ssparse_align>), [`fd_ssparse_footprint`](<#fd_ssparse_footprint>), [`fd_ssparse_new`](<#fd_ssparse_new>), [`fd_ssparse_join`](<#fd_ssparse_join>), and [`fd_ssparse_reset`](<#fd_ssparse_reset>) define the object size, allocate and initialize internal pools and maps, and restore the parser to its initial state. The parser uses an internal manifest map to match account append-vector files to entries in the snapshot manifest, and [`fd_ssparse_populate_acc_vec_map`](<#fd_ssparse_populate_acc_vec_map>) fills that map from slot, id, and file-size arrays. The code exposes a batch mode through [`fd_ssparse_batch_enable`](<#fd_ssparse_batch_enable>), which can group account records when the input layout allows it.
